label: Trip-energy law (LawFinder-style symbolic regression, one formula per powertrain)

compute.notes: 7 time-boxed searches of 20 min wall each on a contended core (s1 ice/hev/bev, s2 ice/hev/bev, s3 plug-in): 0.857 CPU-h incl. constant refits on up to 30,000 train rows; sim-train bands seconds. Scoring the fronts and rungs (ladder.py, evaluate.py) took roughly another 0.5 CPU-h and is not training. One thread, nice 5.

feature_engineering: Seven named trip summaries per row (lawvars.py), identical on both tracks: p / n = positive / negative wheel work per km at the tier's road load, t = minutes per km, m = mass (t), T = mean ambient C, c = start state (-1 warm, 0 unknown, +1 cold), d = km (+ dyn = dynamometer flag in the s2 search, f = plug-in charge-depleting share in s3). Table: read from EnergyNet's 151 inputs (route vector, physics vector, vehicle vector). Trace: recomputed from the trace + spec + rl with EnergyNet's own physics integrals (enet_features.py = byte copy of features.py; equal to the table to 1.2e-4 in log). Target per km e = y / d, loss = squared log error.
rule: keep a rung if its sim val skill beats the incumbent by > 0.01 AND its dev D16 (table track) is not worse than the incumbent's by more than 0.01 (EnergyNet's model-rung rule, the harness's suggestion; stated in src/rungs_formula.py before any rung was scored). Within a rung, laws are chosen on simulations only (knee or lowest sim val median |log error| of the group).

rungs.change: search s1 (7 variables p, n, t, m, T, c, d; 20 min per group): the knee of each group's Pareto front (LawFinder's rule, simulations only): ice c5 e = 3.37 p + t; hev c5 e = 3.321 p + 0.253; bev c16 e = p - n + n exp(-0.0395 T) + 0.0294 m t; plug-ins f E_bev + (1 - f) E_hev
search s1: the most accurate law of each front (lowest sim val median |log error| of the group): ice c21, hev c22, bev c20

search s2 adds the dynamometer-test flag dyn as a law variable; per group the most accurate law on the union of the s1 and s2 fronts: ice s2 c18 e = (p (exp(c/2) - dyn + 3.671))^0.817 + t ln(m + 0.277), hev s1 c22 (unchanged), bev s2 c24
rungs.why: sim val skill 0.3219 does not beat r1's 0.3226 by more than 0.01 (dynamometer trips are 9 % of the sim val set, so the median-based skill cannot see the dyn term), although dev D16 is much better: 0.1518 vs 0.1752 (EPA conv HWY 0.262 -> 0.096, FTP 0.194 -> 0.108, ICCT 0.398 -> 0.196; VED ICE 0.098 -> 0.133, EPA bev HWY 0.109 -> 0.185 worse). Rule kept as stated.

searched_without_rung.s3: a dedicated plug-in law (vars + f, 20 min): no member beats r1's mixing rule on simulated plug-in trips (best median |log error| 0.337 vs 0.315; road-load 0.340), so no rung was built (work/ladder_s3_phev.json)
